units.summary: Test now builds a two-step breaker to match the new groupBreaker type. Test-only change tracking the production type switch.
units.headline: Test uses two-step circuit breaker constructor
units.reason: Test-only constructor swap to match the new breaker type; cannot affect production behavior.

units.summary: Test now builds a two-step breaker to match the new groupBreaker type. Test-only change tracking the production type switch.
units.headline: Test uses two-step circuit breaker constructor
units.reason: Test-only constructor swap to match the new breaker type; cannot affect production behavior.

units.summary: routerMetrics gains a longRunning gauge vec for watches, and its doc comment is updated. Struct field changes feed the exported metrics set.
units.headline: routerMetrics gains a long-running watch gauge
units.reason: Adds a struct field that changes which metrics are exposed; paired with registration and instrument changes.
focus: longRunning is registered and used consistently with instrument

units.summary: Watches are now counted in a per-group long-running gauge and excluded from the duration histogram and in-flight gauge; the duration histogram gains a verb label. The verb label falls back to the raw lowercased HTTP method for non-resource paths.

issues.title: Verb metric label can take arbitrary client-supplied values
issues.failure_scenario: A client sends requests with arbitrary HTTP method tokens (e.g. FOO1, FOO2) to a non-resource path such as /apis/<group>; requestVerb returns the lowercased method, so each distinct method creates a new histogram series, defeating the unknown-group cardinality guard.

units.headline: Watches tracked in long-running gauge, not duration histogram
units.reason: Changes request instrumentation, metric labels and logging flow with defers and a new label dimension on an existing histogram.
focus: verb label cardinality for arbitrary HTTP methods
dashboards or alerts relying on the status_code-only histogram labels
watch access log still emitted on panic or abort

units.summary: GrafanaRouter gets a context and cancel func used to end all watches at shutdown. The comment's claim that it ends every watch holds for watches served through serveWatch.
units.headline: GrafanaRouter gets router-wide watch cancellation context
units.reason: New struct fields drive shutdown and concurrency behavior for long-lived requests.
focus: every path that serves a watch goes through serveWatch
fields are initialized in NewGrafanaRouter for routers built another way

units.summary: Upgrade requests to routed groups are now rejected with 400, and watch requests run through serveWatch so they end when the backend is replaced or the router stops. Non-watch requests are unchanged.
units.headline: Routed groups reject upgrades and scope watches to backend
units.reason: Changes request handling: new 400 response for upgrades and cancellation semantics for watches.
focus: clients that previously proxied WebSocket upgrades through routed groups
watch ending when a backend is replaced and the client re-watch behavior
breaker accounting for watches ended by the router

units.summary: The fallback handler path now rejects upgrades with 400 and wraps watches in serveWatch with only the router-wide scope. Other requests go straight to the handler as before.
units.headline: Fallback path rejects upgrades and scopes watches to router
units.reason: Alters request handling for the single-tenant fallback, including a new 400 for upgrade requests.
focus: fallback clients relying on upgrade support
watch cancellation on router stop for fallback watches

units.summary: New file: classifies requests by Kubernetes verb via RequestInfoFactory, rejects Connection: Upgrade requests, and runs watches under a context cancelled by backend replacement or router shutdown, converting ErrAbortHandler panics into a clean stream end when the router ended the watch.
units.headline: Add watch lifecycle, verb detection and upgrade rejection
units.reason: New concurrency and panic-recovery logic on the request path of every watch.
focus: recover swallows ErrAbortHandler only when the router cancelled and the client did not
requestVerb fallback to the raw HTTP method for non-resource paths
closeWatches really ends all in-flight watches including those started after close
